title: Mars — Planetary Correspondences
parts: Cosmic meaning, spiritual hierarchies and Earth evolution
Human evolution and the journey of the soul
Atlantean oracles, Buddha’s mission and life between incarnations
Constitution, soul, freedom and source-specific organ relations
Metal, nature, art, cycles and symbolic diagrams

chapters.title: What Mars means in Steiner’s cosmology
chapters.short: Visible globe, spiritual individuality, planetary principle, Sun and motion

sub.title: Visible planet, spiritual individuality and planetary principle
sub.body: Mars can denote the physical planet, a spiritual individuality or an occult planetary principle; these are distinct senses.

sub.title: Planetary relationships and the Sun
sub.body: Steiner uses the Sun to differentiate planetary polarities, and gives Mars a distinctive cosmic-speech quality.

sub.title: Cosmic harmony, tone and motion
sub.body: The 1907–08 sources disagree on Mars ratios: Stuttgart and Hanover show 2:1 while Cologne shows 1:2. The contradiction remains unresolved.

sub.title: Observed motion and historical claims about matter
sub.body: GA 323 discusses apparent retrograde motion; GA 354 describes a jelly-like physical Mars, an assertion contradicted by modern astronomy.

chapters.title: Spiritual hierarchies and beings
chapters.short: Dynamis, other hierarchies, Samael, Michael and Cosmic Speech

sub.title: Spirits of Motion, Spirits of Form and wider hierarchies
sub.body: GA 110 places the outer Dynamis or Spirits of Motion boundary at Mars; GA 136 describes wider hierarchy participation.

sub.title: Planetary intelligence, Samael and Michael
sub.body: Samael administers the intelligence of Mars in GA 237, distinct from Dynamis and from the Genius/Demon picture of GA 228.

sub.title: Mars beings, cosmic speech and moral perception
sub.body: GA 231 calls Mars beings guardians of the Cosmic Word; GA 239 characterizes word-beings made of sounding activity.

sub.title: The Thrones and karmic formation
sub.body: The Thrones take part in a Mars phase of karmic shaping in GA 239; this is different from a hierarchy boundary.

chapters.title: Cosmic evolution and the Mars phase of Earth
chapters.short: Old Moon, Mars/Mercury halves, iron and blood

sub.title: Old Moon, recapitulation and the formation of Mars
sub.body: Present Mars is a higher Old Moon recurrence in GA 13; early planetary separation occurs within Earth recapitulation in GA 109/112.

sub.title: The Mars and Mercury phases of Earth
sub.body: The earlier and later portions of Earth evolution are sometimes called Mars and Mercury, representing strength and wisdom, while Earth develops love.

sub.title: Displaced souls and the return to Earth
sub.body: Steiner describes some human souls temporarily dwelling in other planetary spheres, including Mars, before returning to Earth.

sub.title: Iron, blood and the development of human faculties
sub.body: A Martian iron narrative is linked to warm red blood, courage, an instrument of the I and the later transformation of aggression.

chapters.title: Human history and initiation
chapters.short: Atlantean Mars Oracle, Rishis, cultural periods and retrospect

sub.title: Lemurian return and the Atlantean Mars Oracle
sub.body: The Atlantean Mars Oracle appears within a wider system led by the Sun Oracle; it is esoteric, not established archaeology.

sub.title: The Rishis, historical decans and cultural epochs
sub.body: The Rishis synthesize planetary Oracle streams; no securely named Mars Rishi is established by this passage.

sub.title: Early modern science and the Mars crisis
sub.body: GA 130 attributes impulses of early modern science to Mars experience and describes a cultural crisis before the 1604 Buddha mission.

sub.title: Mars mysteries and the life retrospect
sub.body: GA 239 connects the Mars chapter of a retrospective life tableau with ages 42–49, looked back upon later in life.

sub.title: Critical context for historical racial typologies
sub.body: Steiner’s racial-essentialist planetary typologies are scientifically unsupported and belong only to critically annotated archival history.

chapters.title: Buddha, Christ and the transformation of Mars
chapters.short: The 1604 mission and the transformation of combative forces

sub.title: Earlier Mars activity and the planetary crisis
sub.body: Steiner describes earlier combative Martian forces and a subsequent spiritual crisis in the sphere.

sub.title: The mission of Buddha and Christian Rosenkreutz
sub.body: GA 130 narrates Christian Rosenkreutz’s spiritual assembly and Buddha’s 1604 Mars deed, analogous but not identical to Christ’s deed on Earth.

sub.title: Peace, inwardness and life between incarnations
sub.body: Mars is described as communicating renewed inward peace and independence from conformist opinion after Buddha’s deed.

chapters.title: Between death and a new birth
chapters.short: Outer spheres, cosmic speech, karmic review and return to birth

sub.title: The outward journey and access to the outer spheres
sub.body: The after-death journey goes beyond Sun to Mars, Jupiter and Saturn; GA 227 limits what present humanity can fully attain.

sub.title: Cosmic speech and the formation of a spiritual Mars organ
sub.body: Cosmic music becomes Cosmic Word in Mars; a postmortem spiritual organ is compared to lungs and larynx, not equated with them.

sub.title: Karmic review and named biographies
sub.body: The outer spheres participate in karmic shaping. Mars-linked cases such as Voltaire are individual esoteric biographies, not universal destinies.

sub.title: Return toward birth, will and preparation for speech
sub.body: Mars is connected with future will, chest and limbs and speech preparation, alongside Venus in the pre-birth account.

chapters.title: Human constitution, soul and freedom
chapters.short: Astral organization, dated soul charts and ethical initiative

sub.title: Astral organization, the I and the consciousness pole
sub.body: Mars is part of astral and outer-planet consciousness accounts; it is not an exclusive assignment of the human I.

sub.title: Soul members across dated sources and editions
sub.body: 1905/1908 sources link Mars with sentient soul, while GA 317’s 1924 prose and German 1995 chart link Mars to mind soul. Online charts disagree.

sub.title: Temperament, courage, initiative and moral freedom
sub.body: GA 213 distinguishes Mars-linked character-bound initiative from conscious moral intuition; GA 151 associates Mars with Voluntarism.

sub.title: Sleep, speech and creative thought
sub.body: GA 119 names Mars as a sleep threshold force; GA 228 describes only qualified freedom in speech; notes show a Venus–Mars–Jupiter creative relation.

chapters.title: Organs, life processes and bodily correspondences
chapters.short: Gallbladder, voice, breathing, blood, lymph and left ear

sub.title: Inner organ map: gallbladder, bile and nourishment
sub.body: The gallbladder is inner Mars in GA 107 and GA 128, placed beside heart/Sun, liver/Jupiter and spleen/Saturn in a symbolic organ system.

sub.title: Larynx, lungs, breathing and rhythmic processes
sub.body: GA 128 gives upper Mars/iron to larynx but inner lungs to Mercury. Other sources give Mars breathing and a postmortem lung-larynx analogy.

sub.title: Blood, circulation, lymph and blood formation
sub.body: Mars/iron/blood and Mars/lymph are separate source claims; another sevenfold organ table assigns blood formation to Venus.

sub.title: Sense organization and the left ear
sub.body: GA 218 groups Mars with outer-planet sense work; GA 91’s 1904 meditation notes give Mars to the left ear symbolically.

sub.title: Historical medicine and curative education
sub.body: Mars–iron metal tables and horoscope-based curative-education cases are historical claims, not valid tools for diagnosis or prescribing.

chapters.title: Iron, metals and Earth substances
chapters.short: Planetary metal links, iron in blood and historical medical uses

sub.title: Iron, Earth and cosmic substance
sub.body: Mars–iron is explicit in medical and mystery metal lists and appears in an esoteric origin narrative for Earth substance.

sub.title: Blood color, bodily activity and plant development
sub.body: The iron/red-blood link is distinct from outer-planet metal influences on flower and seed development in GA 312.

sub.title: Mystery-school and historical medical applications
sub.body: Historical correspondences of Mars and iron must not be used to justify unsupervised supplements or treatments.

chapters.title: Plants, animals and agriculture
chapters.short: Group souls, insects, silica pathways, oak and red rose

sub.title: Animal forms, group souls and the zodiac
sub.body: GA 136 places differentiated animal group-soul activity in several planetary regions, modulated by zodiacal positions.

sub.title: Insects, caterpillars and metamorphosis
sub.body: GA 230 gives Mars-caterpillar analogies and GA 354 a long insect development claim; neither is established biology.

sub.title: Plant development, soil and food-forming processes
sub.body: Outer Mars/Jupiter/Saturn together are said to act through silica-rich soil; other lectures link planetary motion with plant spirals.

sub.title: Oak, red rose and limits of agricultural application
sub.body: An oak planting period and a red rose are described under Mars; no validated agricultural scheduling or pigment rule follows.

chapters.title: Speech, music, art and philosophy
chapters.short: Cosmic Word, musical schemes, eurythmy and Voluntarism

sub.title: Cosmic speech, human language and development
sub.body: Mars is a spiritual sphere of speech and works with Venus in one pre-birth account; astrological language effects are not scientifically demonstrated.

sub.title: Musical order, tone and the human instrument
sub.body: The separate 1908 Q&A gives c–iron–Mars; GA 104a places Mars fourth in another sevenfold musical scheme. Do not merge them.

sub.title: Eurythmy, gestures and poetic expressions
sub.body: Specific exercises relate Mars to vowel E, outward gestures and a planetary line in the Twelve Moods.

sub.title: Worldview and artistic interpretation
sub.body: GA 151 maps Mars to the philosophical Voluntarism mood and insists this is not a natal horoscope system.

chapters.title: Time cycles, ritual and symbolic diagrams
chapters.short: Tuesday, esoteric red, Samael and Tree of Life boundaries

sub.title: Tuesday, life stages and sevenfold sequences
sub.body: Tuesday is associated with Mars; the initiatory 42–49-year chapter represents a different sevenfold structure.

sub.title: Red, iron, Samael and esoteric diagrams
sub.body: Esoteric notes pair Mars with red, iron, Samael, courage and a particular soul-member hexagram scheme.

sub.title: Astrological diagrams and textual cautions
sub.body: GA 228 sky aspects, GA 151 worldview symbols and GA 317 individual case horoscopes have distinct contexts and evidential limits.

sub.title: Tree of Life navigation and its source boundary
sub.body: Geburah–Mars is the BOTA-derived navigation scheme adopted by this Atlas, not a demonstrated Steiner-authored Tree of Life assignment.
